sources.snippet: ABSTRACT This work proves that ranks and shares are statistically dependent on one another, based on simple combinatorics. It presents a formula for rank-share distribution and illustrates that Zipf's law, is descended from expected values of various ranks in the new distribution. sources.snippet: Zipf's law (/ zɪf /) is an empirical law stating that when a set of measured values is sorted in decreasing order, the value of the n -th entry is often approximately inversely proportional to n. sources.title: Zipf's Law and Cache Hit Ratios: Why Your Caching Math Fails When ...
sources.snippet: We assume that web traffic naturally obeys Zipf's Law. When real-world traffic breaks that assumption due to bot activity, cryptographic lookups, or flash crowds—standard cache sizing formulas completely fall apart. Let's look at why cache math relies on power-law distributions and what happens when reality refuses to cooperate.
